candidates.locator: Chapter 21.1 — Of Religious Worship, and the Sabbath Day
candidates.phrase: there is a God, who hath lordship and sovereignty over all
candidates.rationale: Directly asserts that God possesses lordship and sovereignty over all, matching the authority/sovereignty floor.
candidates.chunk_text: The light of nature showeth that there is a God, who hath lordship and sovereignty over all, is good, and doth good unto all, and is therefore to be feared, loved, praised, called upon, trusted in, and served, with all the heart, and with all the soul, and with all the might. But the acceptable way of worshiping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited by his own revealed will, that he may not be worshiped according to the imaginations and devices of men, or the suggestions of Satan, under any visible representation, or any other way not prescribed in the Holy Scripture.

candidates.phrase: God, the supreme Lord and King of all the world
candidates.rationale: Confession names God as the supreme Lord and King of all the world, asserting sovereign authority over creation.
candidates.chunk_text: God, the supreme Lord and King of all the world, hath ordained civil magistrates, to be, under him, over the people, for his own glory, and the public good: and, to this end, hath armed them with the power of the sword, for the defense and encouragement of them that are good, and for the punishment of evildoers.

candidates.locator: Book of Confessions 6.112 (Westminster Confession of Faith)
candidates.phrase: there is a God, who hath lordship and sovereignty over all
candidates.rationale: Parallel PC(USA) edition asserts God's lordship and sovereignty over all as a divine attribute.
candidates.chunk_text: 1. The light of nature showeth that there is a God, who hath lordship and sovereignty over all; is good, and doeth good unto all; and is therefore to be feared, loved, praised, called upon, trusted in, and served with all the heart, and with all the soul, and with all the might. But the acceptable way of worshipping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited by his own revealed will, that he may not be worshipped according to the imaginations and devices of men, or the suggestions of Satan, under any visible representation or any other way not prescribed in the Holy Scripture. h Ed. 1647 includes: “and by the Power of the Civil Magistrate.” Presbyterian Church in the United States The United Presbyterian Church in the United States of America
